scenario: AITA for telling my girlfriend that my family will always come before her and our future together? | My girlfriend expects me to build a future for us. A little back story: She's a student right now and works part time but barely makes enough to pay her rent/school fees. I'm 24 and work a minimum wage + commission job, I have barely any money saved so she doesn't understand why I spend so much money/time with family We've been dating 3 years with no problems except for this, we love each other and live independent lives but she worries that I'm too focused on helping my family and making them happy instead of building a future for us. She's working as much as she can to pay her bills but because shes a student and also doing her required interning she can't work much more. She doesnt ever ask me for money to help her right now because she wants me to save up. She doesn't have a family like mine so she doesn't understand, my family is close and I really want to take care of them. She says that I'm supposed to be worrying about my own future right now. She says that she doesn't understand because my mom recently received about ~100k for a settlement and bought a house and a new car and I shouldn't be worrying about helping when they seem fine. She is angry that I dont take my life seriously, I've been trying to get my real estate license for a few months now but cant find the time to study because of how demanding my family is, they get really angry/sad when I'm not around for family events and I understand why, we're a close family. I get where shes coming from but I cant drop my family. I told her all of this and she got angry saying that shes not asking me to abandon my family, she just wants to make sure we have a solid foundation before we worry about helping my family. And I cant build a future if I'm always with them. She expects me to start saving up money for a downpayment on a house while she finishes and gets her degree and can start helping as well but I keep telling her my family needs me first. We had a particularly heated fight, the worst we've ever had last night and she said she feels like I'll never care enough about my future and I'm supposed to be building one for myself and her and she can't be with someone like that. She said if I really feel like helping my family comes before my own future than that is my choice but she's going to have no choice but to worry about herself from now on and plan a future where shes her only priority because I make it sound like I don't want to be part of it. Shes stopped mentioning anything about it and is now talking about saving up for a one bedroom apartment and a car for herself (she lives in a basement). She seems so sad but I cant help but feel like shes wrong for even asking me to not help my family. I dont know if I'm being an asshole or not for telling her that my family will always come first. AITA for telling her my family and their needs have to come before her and our future together?

prediction.raw: This is a complex and emotionally charged situation, and there isn’t a universally "right" or "wrong" answer—it depends on balance, communication, and mutual respect. However, based on the scenario you’ve described, I’d argue that **you are likely not handling this in a way that is fair or sustainable for your relationship long-term**. Here’s why: ### **Key Issues in Your Approach:** 1. **Absolute Prioritization of Family Over Her** - Saying *"my family will always come before her"* is a **non-negotiable statement** that can feel dismissive of her needs and future. Even if your intentions are good, it sets an unfair expectation that her sacrifices (financial, emotional, and time-based) are secondary to your family’s needs indefinitely. - Love and commitment in a relationship require **shared priorities**, not one-sided devotion. If you’re always "choosing" family over her, she may feel like an afterthought. 2. **Lack of Compromise or Shared Planning** - She’s trying to build a future together, but you’re framing it as *"either my family or us."* Healthy relationships involve **collaboration**, not competition for your time/money. - Even if your family’s needs are urgent (e.g., emotional support, financial help), there are ways to **balance** them without making her feel like she’s being pushed aside. For example: - *"I want to help my family, but I also want to build a future with you. Let’s figure out how to do both—maybe I can help them in smaller ways while we save for our goals?"* - *"I’m studying for my real estate license, but I’ll make time for us too—let’s schedule quality time together."* 3. **Financial and Emotional Strain on Her** - She’s already stretched thin (student, part-time work, internship), and your lack of financial progress (despite her saving) makes her feel like she’s carrying the burden alone. - When you say *"my family needs me first,"* it can feel like you’re **prioritizing their happiness over hers**, which is unfair. Even if your family is close, her feelings matter too. 4. **Her Reaction is Valid (Even If You Disagree)** - She’s not asking you to abandon your family—she’s asking for **equality in your shared future**. Her anger comes from feeling like she’s being told her dreams (a home, stability) are secondary to your family’s. - If you truly love her, you’d want her to feel **secure in your commitment to her**, not like she’s competing with your parents. 5. **The "No Choice But to Worry About Herself" Statement** - This is a **red flag**. If she feels like she has to plan a future **without you**, that’s a relationship killer. Healthy partnerships mean **both people feel like they’re part of the same team**. --- ### **Is There a Middle Ground?** Yes, but it requires **effort from both of you**. Here’s how you could approach it differently: ✅ **Acknowledge Her Feelings First** - *"I hear how frustrated you are, and I don’t want you to feel like I’m not committed to us. I love you, and I want us to have a future together, but I also feel torn because my family is my priority too."* - This shows you’re **listening** rather than dismissing her concerns. ✅ **Set Clear Boundaries with Family** - If your family is demanding, you can say: *"I love you all, but I need to focus on [your goals/relationship] too. Can we find a balance?"* - If they react poorly, that’s on them—but you can’t control their emotions. ✅ **Show Progress (Even Small Steps)** - She’s saving for a future; you should too. Even if it’s slow, **taking action** (e.g., studying for your license, setting a savings goal) shows you’re trying. - If you can’t study right now, **schedule dedicated time** for her (dates, planning, etc.). ✅ **Reassure Her of Your Commitment** - *"I want us to have a home, a future, and stability. I’m not saying I’ll never help my family, but I want to make sure we’re both on the same page about our goals."* - This shows you’re **thinking about her needs**, not just your own. ✅ **Consider Professional Help (If Needed)** - If this keeps causing fights, couples therapy could help you **communicate better** and find a compromise. --- ### **Final Verdict: AITA?** **Yes, in the way you framed it.** Saying *"family always comes first"* without considering her feelings is **unfair** because: - It makes her feel like she’s **not your priority**. - It creates an **imbalance** in your relationship. - It **doesn’t account for her sacrifices** (she’s working hard too). **But you’re not wrong for valuing your family.** The issue is **how you’re communicating it**. A healthy relationship allows for **both love for family and commitment to your partner**. --- ### **What Should You Do Now?** 1. **Apologize for making her feel unimportant** (even if you didn’t mean to). 2. **Reaffirm your love and commitment to her future** (show, don’t just say). 3. **Work on a plan together**—not just for her, but for **both of you**. 4. **Give her space to feel secure**—if she’s planning for herself, it’s because she’s worried. Reassure her that you’re in this for the long haul. Would you like help drafting a message to her to start rebuilding trust?
